messages.subject: Multi-season: changes in occupancy
parts:
Hi everybody, I hope this email finds you healthy and well.

I'm running multi-season occupancy models using the function colext() of the "unmarked".

I've successfully extracted the parameters psi1, gamma, epsilon and p. However, I'm interested in the lambda, rate of change in occupancy by period (seasons).

Does anyone know how to extract the psi for each period, to see how psi has changed over time?

Thank you very much for your help!

Kind regards.
Roberta

Att.

Msc. Roberta Montanheiro Paolino
PhD student in Applied Ecology
Conservation and Ecology Lab of Ribeirão Preto (LAEC) - FFCLRP/USP

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Re: Multi-season: changes in occupancy
parts:
You can get psi for each season using projected(model) where model is your fitted colext model.
-G

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Multi-season: changes in occupancy
parts:
Hi Roberta,

I believe you'd just want to use the probability of occupancy (the probability of unoccupied is simply 1 - occupancy).

I neglected to note that you can also extract site-specific (rather than mean) projected occupancy and generate site-specific estimated latent occupancy state.

Site-specific projected occupancy can be obtained using t(projected(model,mean="F")[2,,]). This retrieves the projected occupancy array from your model and transposes it so that rows = sites and columns = seasons.

The posterior distribution of the latent occupancy state is an estimate of true occupancy (which also incorporates information about known occupancy if the species was detected) and can be generated using bup(ranef(model),stat = 'mean') or bup(ranef(model),stat = 'mode') (returning only 1s and 0s). Like the above,  rows = sites and columns = seasons.

- Giancarlo
